subject: SLO program kickoff: tiered SLOs + error budgets (Hosted + Dedicated)
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, Jan 10, 2026 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: SLO program kickoff: tiered SLOs + error budgets (Hosted + Dedicated)

Hi Ethan, Lauren, Marissa,

We’re kicking off the reliability program to formalize tiered SLOs (Hosted API vs Dedicated) and make error budgets operational (alerting + release/rollout enforcement). I’d like to align on objectives, scope boundaries, and initial owners so we can publish a canonical spec quickly and avoid re-litigating definitions during incidents.

Meeting
- When: Tue, Jan 15, 10:00–11:00am PT
- Where: Zoom (link in calendar invite)
- Prep: skim the draft page + add comments/questions (10 min)

Objectives (what we need to leave with)
1) Agreement on tier principles
   - What “Hosted” reliability means (multi-tenant, broader model mix)
   - What “Dedicated” reliability means (isolation + capacity commitments)
   - What’s explicitly excluded from SLI accounting (invalid auth, customer-side timeouts, etc.)

2) Target deliverables for Phase 0/1 (Jan–Feb)
   - Tiered SLO table for key journeys (chat/completions streaming + non-streaming, embeddings, catalog ops)
   - Dedicated-specific indicators (pool readiness / provision-to-ready) and how we’ll measure them safely
   - Error budget policy (burn-rate thresholds, escalation, and what changes when budgets are at risk/exhausted)

3) Initial ownership + timeline
   - SLO definitions/spec authoring: Aisha Bello (SRE) w/ review from Platform + Product
   - Error budget enforcement mechanics (gates, canaries, routing degradation): Platform leads (control plane/routing) with SRE partnership
   - Console visibility requirements (MVP): Marissa team to define surfaces + permissions assumptions

Proposed agenda
- 10 min: context + why now (recent incidents where we learned too late)
- 15 min: tier principles + exclusions (where we tend to drift)
- 20 min: SLO/SLI strawman (streaming, timeouts, disconnect taxonomy, latency p95/p99)
- 10 min: error budget policy (what “at risk” and “exhausted” mean in practice)
- 5 min: owners, immediate next steps, and Phase 0 milestones

Draft doc (add comments inline)
- Confluence (draft): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/SLOs+and+Error+Budgets+-+Kickoff+Draft
- Working folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1sre-slo-program-kickoff

Two calls I want leadership input on up front
- Streaming latency SLI: do we anchor on TTFT vs full stream duration (or both) per tier?
- Dedicated readiness: what customer-facing expectation do we want to set for “pool ready” (and how do we handle scaling lag)?

If you can’t make it, please reply with a delegate who can speak for priorities/tradeoffs (especially around what we’re willing to block during budget burn).

Thanks,
Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference


From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 10, 2026 at 9:27 AM PT
Subject: Re: SLO program kickoff: tiered SLOs + error budgets (Hosted + Dedicated)

I’m in.

One suggestion: we should explicitly cover “what gets gated” in Phase 1 vs Phase 2 so teams don’t assume we’re hard-blocking deploys immediately. Happy to have control plane bring a proposal (warn-only → soft block).

Also +1 on separating TTFT vs stream duration.

-Ethan


From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 10, 2026 at 10:08 AM PT
Subject: Re: SLO program kickoff: tiered SLOs + error budgets (Hosted + Dedicated)

Confirmed.

For Dedicated: can we make sure we cover (a) pool readiness/provision-to-ready definition and (b) how we communicate during a readiness dip vs an active incident? We’ve had customers conflate “autoscaling lag” with “outage.”

I’ll add a couple examples to the draft page later today.

-Lauren


From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 10, 2026 at 11:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: SLO program kickoff: tiered SLOs + error budgets (Hosted + Dedicated)

I can make it.

From Console perspective: would love clarity on what dimensions we’re committing to expose in MVP (tier/region/model/route) vs what stays internal initially (customer-specific Dedicated views). If we decide early, it’ll save us a bunch of rework on permissions.

Will comment on the draft.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole
Director of Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference
